cases.prompt:
ok we're finally doing the refund flow rewrite. can you help me write an intent for it? the slug should be refund-flow-v2.

context: right now refunds go through a legacy stripe integration and the CX team keeps complaining that partial refunds break the ledger — the ledger entry gets created for the full amount even when only $20 of a $50 charge was refunded, so month-end reconciliation is a nightmare and finance manually adjusts ~30 entries per month. we also can't refund past 90 days (stripe limit) but customers keep asking. product wants us to move to our own refund ledger with proper partial-refund support and a 12-month window backed by store credit for the 90+ day cases.

the project is a rails 7 monorepo with a react admin surface. audit trail matters — SOC2 audit is in Q2.
cases.quality_criteria: Captures WHY (business/user pain, timing, downstream cost); captures WHO for; scopes the problem without designing the solution; surfaces open questions for spec/plan; does NOT prematurely commit to implementation choices; frontmatter with status: draft.

cases.prompt:
we just had a P1. checkout was returning 500s intermittently between 14:02 and 14:47 UTC today (2026-09-01). Sentry shows the traceback pointing at CouponService#apply — nil error on `code.expires_at`. datadog shows a spike in latency on the coupons-db read replica starting 13:58 UTC, right after the marketing team's flash-sale campaign went live at 13:55.

rollback: the ops team disabled the flash-sale coupon at 14:47 and errors stopped. we haven't deployed anything since yesterday morning.

can you diagnose read-only and turn this into whatever the playbook wants us to produce so we can actually fix this through the normal review flow? don't touch code — I want the audit trail intact.
cases.quality_criteria: Priority order: (1) read-only diagnosis, no code touched; (2) audit trail preserved; (3) produces the artifact needed to re-enter the fix through the normal review flow; (4) captures evidence and hypothesis clearly.

cases.prompt:
we're doing a schema migration on the tenants table next sprint — need to split `tenants.settings` (currently a JSONB blob) into a proper `tenant_settings` table with a foreign key, because we now have 40+ settings keys and querying by any of them requires JSONB GIN scans that are killing p99 on the admin dashboard.

the complication: `tenants.settings` contains a `pii_export_policy` key that the compliance team owns (they audit it quarterly), a `billing_defaults` key that finance owns, and a `feature_flags` sub-object that pretty much every team writes to.

I want to run this through the full three-artifact regime because it's touching PII surface, migrations, and cross-team ownership. start with the intent — I'll come back for spec once product signs off.
cases.quality_criteria: (1) Intent-stage discipline — captures why, does NOT design the migration; (2) names policy owners (compliance, finance) as reviewers up front; (3) surfaces high-risk nature (PII + migration → escalation to tech lead / architect per approval matrix); (4) lists spec-stage open questions rather than answering them.
